answer: Each new agent identity must be grafted onto an existing sponsor vine: the sponsor locks a slashable bond that stays frozen until the recruit completes N epochs of unique, attestable work. A public randomness beacon then samples pairs of vines for correlated behavior (shared keys, synchronized timing, identical answer hashes). If a cluster is found, every bond on that vine is burned and the sponsor's reward zenith is permanently capped, so an attacker who mints many fakes pays a linear bond loss plus a lasting ceiling on what the whole cluster can ever earn.
